Common issues and questions when working with the Neuroglancer scenes and Dash
Apps. Click a question to expand it. If something is not covered here, contact
your instructor or TA, or
[report an issue](https://github.com/AllenInstitute/Teaching_Connectomics/issues/new).

::: {#browser .callout-note collapse="true"}
## Which browser should I use?

Use **Google Chrome** or **Mozilla Firefox**. **Avoid Safari** — it sometimes
fails to render the Neuroglancer scene, or will not let you copy Root IDs into or
out of the viewer. If a scene or Dash App is misbehaving, switching to Chrome or
Firefox is the first thing to try.
:::

::: {#login .callout-note collapse="true"}
## I am asked to log in — what do I do?

When you open a Neuroglancer scene or a Dash App you may be prompted to log in.
Click **"Request Login"** and sign in with **any Google account**. To activate
your access you must also accept the MICrONS Terms of Service, which you only need
to do once per account:

> Accept the TOS here: <https://global.daf-apis.com/sticky_auth/api/v1/tos/2/accept>
:::

::: {#render .callout-note collapse="true"}
## The segmentation or meshes do not render

If neurons or meshes do not appear in a scene, follow these steps:

1. Accept the Terms of Service on your Google-authorized account:
   <https://global.daf-apis.com/sticky_auth/api/v1/tos/2/accept>
2. Hard-refresh your Neuroglancer window.
3. If the right-hand segmentation panel still shows a red error message, contact
   your instructor or TA.

If only a specific neuron fails to render, see
[A Root ID does not appear](#root-ids) below, and confirm you are using a
[recommended browser](#browser).
:::

::: {#versions .callout-note collapse="true"}
## What is a dataset "version" (materialization)?

The MICrONS dataset is **continuously proofread**, so the reconstruction changes
over time. To keep results reproducible, the data is periodically frozen into
numbered snapshots called **materialization versions**. Each version fixes the
segmentation, the Root IDs, and the annotation tables at a single moment in time.

These modules use **version v1300** so that every student sees the same cells and
the same Root IDs. Newer versions — including the **"Latest"** option in the Dash
Apps — contain more proofreading, but their Root IDs differ from v1300.
:::

::: {#graphene .callout-note collapse="true"}
## Static vs. dynamic (Graphene) segmentation

The dataset has two kinds of segmentation layer:

- **Static (flat) layer** — a frozen segmentation for a single version. The module
  Neuroglancer scenes use the **v1300 static layer**. It loads quickly, never
  changes, and its Root IDs match v1300. This is what the module links use.
- **Dynamic (Graphene) layer** — the live, editable segmentation that reflects the
  most recent proofreading. Its Root IDs can change as cells are merged or split.
  **Neuroglancer links generated from the Dash Apps use the Graphene layer**, so
  they show the latest data, not v1300.

Because of this, a Root ID copied from a v1300 scene can differ from the "same"
cell's Root ID in a Graphene / latest scene. The Dash Apps handle this
substitution automatically — see [the yellow warning](#warning).
:::

::: {#root-ids .callout-note collapse="true"}
## A Root ID does not appear, or has no mesh or synapses

Every neuron has a unique **Root ID**, but proofreading edits create new Root IDs
over time, so a Root ID that is valid in one version may not be valid in another.
In a Neuroglancer scene this can show up as a neuron with no mesh, or a cell with
no synapses. If that happens:

- Try a different Root ID, **or**
- Make sure the version you are viewing matches the version the Root ID came from.

This mismatch is a normal consequence of the dataset being updated; it does not
mean you did anything wrong.
:::

::: {#warning .callout-note collapse="true"}
## What is the yellow warning in the Dash Apps?

When you enter a Root ID in a Dash App (the Table Viewer or the Connectivity
Viewer) that is not valid at the selected **Materialization** version, the app
automatically looks up the most-overlapping valid Root ID and shows *that* cell's
data, along with a **yellow warning banner**. This warning is **expected and
intended** — it tells you the app substituted the correct Root ID for the version
you queried, so you do not need to do anything about it.

![The Table Viewer warns when a Root ID is not valid at the queried version and shows the most-overlapping valid Root ID instead.](resources/module_4_dash_table_warning.png)

The **Materialization** dropdown defaults to **"Latest."** If you want your Dash
App results to match the cells shown in the module scenes, select **v1300**.
:::
